verify_note: CE 2.44–2.46 read: Guha is king and Rama's friend (2.44.9-12); Lakshmana washes Rama's feet that night (2.44.25); Guha keeps watch (2.44.26); at dawn Rama sees a boat, boards, boatmen row across (2.46.61-66); Sita prays to Ganga mid-stream (2.46.67-71). Kevat's foot-washing at the boat: Tulsidas, Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand.
caption: Many of us know the boatman Kevat who washed Rama's feet before taking him across the Ganga. Valmiki's Ramayana tells it differently: Guha is a king and Rama's dearest friend, the one who washes Rama's feet that night is Lakshmana, and at dawn Rama simply boards a boat and the boatmen row them across. The Kevat story comes from Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas. The kevat's lovely line is Tulsidas's (Ramcharitmanas, Ayodhya Kand 100.4): “Jau prabhu par avasi ga chahahu, mohi pad padum pakharan kahahu”, “Lord, if you must cross, first let me wash your lotus feet.”

lines: तस्य भूमौ शयानस्य पादौ प्रक्षाल्य लक्ष्मणः ।
sloka.en: “Lakshmana washed the feet of Rama, who lay on the ground with his wife, then stood leaning on a tree.”
sloka.translit: tasya bhūmau śayānasya pādau prakṣālya lakṣmaṇaḥ, sabhāryasya tato'bhyetya tasthau vṛkṣamupāśritaḥ

shots.hi: वनवास के रास्ते, राम गंगा किनारे पहुँचते हैं। यहाँ निषादों का राजा गुह रहता है, राम का प्राणों जैसा मित्र।
shots.en: On the way to exile, Rama reaches the Ganga. Here lives Guha, king of the Nishadas, a friend as dear to Rama as his own life.

shots.hi: रघुनंदन, ये धरती भी आपकी है, जैसे अयोध्या। कहिए, मैं आपके लिए क्या करूँ?
shots.en: "Raghunandana, this land is yours, just as Ayodhya is. Tell me, what may I do for you?"

shots.hi: उस रात, राम और सीता ज़मीन पर सोते हैं, और लक्ष्मण, राम के पैर धोते हैं।
shots.en: That night, Rama and Sita sleep on the bare ground, and Lakshmana washes Rama's feet.

shots.hi: गुह और लक्ष्मण, धनुष लिए, रात भर पहरा देते हैं।
shots.en: Guha and Lakshmana, bows in hand, keep watch all night.
units: गुह और लक्ष्मण, धनुष लिए, रात भर पहरा देते हैं।
[serious] पैर धोने वाले थे… [pause] लक्ष्मण।

shots.hi: सुबह, राम किनारे पर एक नाव देखते हैं। मल्लाह पतवार चलाते हैं, और नाव गंगा पार करने लगती है।
shots.en: At dawn, Rama sees a boat at the bank. The boatmen row, and the boat sets out across the Ganga.
units: सुबह, राम किनारे पर एक नाव देखते हैं।

shots.en: In the middle of the Ganga, Sita joins her palms and prays to the river.

claims.claim: Guha, king of the Nishadas, Rama's friend dear as his own self, lived at the Ganga
Guha embraced Rama: 'This place is yours just as Ayodhya; what may I do for you?'
That night Rama and Sita lay on the ground; Lakshmana washed Rama's feet
Guha, bow in hand, stayed awake with Lakshmana guarding Rama
At dawn Rama saw a boat at the bank, boarded with Sita and Lakshmana; boatmen rowed them across
Mid-river Sita joined her palms and prayed to the Ganga
No boatman washes Rama's feet and there is no bargaining at the boat in the CE crossing (2.46)
Kevat washing Rama's feet before the crossing is from Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas (Ayodhya Kand)
